summary: The court had four kinds of death penalty. The Tanna Kamma and Rabbi Shimon list them in different orders, from the most severe to the least.

chunks.en: Four kinds of death penalty were given to the court:
chunks.st: Four types of the death penalty were given over to the court,
chunks.stMore: with which those who committed certain transgressions are executed. They are, in descending order of severity:

chunks.en: stoning, burning,
chunks.st: Stoning, burning,

chunks.en: the sword, and choking.
chunks.st: killing by decapitation, and strangulation.

chunks.en: Rabbi Shimon says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Shimon says: They are, in descending order of severity:

chunks.en: burning, stoning,
chunks.st: Burning, stoning,

chunks.en: choking, and the sword.
chunks.st: strangulation, and killing.

chunks.en: What we learned before is how stoning is done.
chunks.st: This execution, described in the previous chapter, is referring to the mitzva of those who are stoned, i.e., to the process of execution by stoning.

summary: This mishnah tells how the punishment of burning was done by the court. Rabbi Yehudah and Rabbi Elazar ben Tzadok add their opinions.

chunks.en: How the punishment of burning is done:
chunks.st: The mitzva of those who are burned,
chunks.stMore: i.e., the process of execution by burning, is carried out in the following manner:

chunks.he: הָיוּ מְשַׁקְּעִין אוֹתוֹ בַזֶּבֶל עַד אַרְכֻּבּוֹתָיו
chunks.en: They would stand him in soft ground up to his knees,
chunks.st: The executioners submerge the condemned one in dung up to his knees so he cannot move,

chunks.en: and they put a hard cloth inside a soft one
chunks.st: and they place a rough scarf within a soft one, so his throat will not be wounded,

chunks.en: and wrap it around his neck.
chunks.st: and wrap these scarves around his neck.

chunks.he: זֶה מוֹשֵׁךְ אֶצְלוֹ וְזֶה מוֹשֵׁךְ אֶצְלוֹ
chunks.en: This one pulls it toward himself and that one pulls it toward himself
chunks.st: This one, i.e., one of the witnesses, pulls the scarf toward himself, and that one, the other witness, pulls it toward himself,

chunks.en: until he opens his mouth.
chunks.st: until the condemned one is forced to open his mouth, as he is choking.

chunks.en: And he lights a wick
chunks.st: And another person then lights the wick

chunks.en: and puts it into his mouth,
chunks.st: and throws it into his mouth,

chunks.en: and it goes down inside him
chunks.st: and it goes down into his intestines

chunks.en: and burns him inside.
chunks.st: and burns his intestines and he dies.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehudah says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says:

chunks.en: if he died while they were holding him,
chunks.st: But if this one who is condemned to death by burning accidentally died at their hands by strangulation,

chunks.he: לֹא הָיוּ מְקַיְּמִין בּוֹ מִצְוַת שְׂרֵפָה,
chunks.en: they did not do the mitzvah of burning.
chunks.st: they have not fulfilled the mitzva of execution by burning for this person.

chunks.en: Instead, they open his mouth with tongs
chunks.st: Rather, the process is carried out in the following manner: One opens the mouth of the condemned person with prongs,

chunks.en: against his will,
chunks.st: against his will,

chunks.en: and he lights the wick
chunks.st: and one lights the wick

chunks.en: and puts it into his mouth,
chunks.st: and throws it into his mouth,

chunks.he: וְיוֹרֶדֶת לְתוֹךְ מֵעָיו וְחוֹמֶרֶת אֶת בְּנֵי מֵעָיו.
chunks.en: and it goes down inside him and burns him.
chunks.st: and it goes down into his intestines and burns his intestines and he dies.

chunks.en: Rabbi Elazar ben Tzadok said,
chunks.st: Rabbi Elazar ben Tzadok said:

chunks.en: "Once a daughter of a Kohen did a terrible sin,
chunks.st: An incident occurred with regard to a certain priest’s daughter who committed adultery,

chunks.en: and they put bundles of branches around her and burned her."
chunks.st: and they wrapped her in bundles of branches and burned her,
chunks.stMore: contrary to the process described in the mishna.

chunks.en: They said to him,
chunks.st: The Sages said to him: That court did not act properly; they did so

chunks.en: "That was because the court
chunks.st: because the court

chunks.en: of that time did not know the halachah well."
chunks.st: at that time was not proficient in halakha.

summary: This mishnah tells how the punishments of the sword and of choking were done by the court.

chunks.en: How the punishment of the sword is done:
chunks.st: The mitzva of those who are killed,
chunks.stMore: i.e., the process of execution by decapitation, is carried out in the following manner:

chunks.en: They would cut off his head with a sword,
chunks.st: The executioners cut off his head with a sword,

chunks.en: the way the kingdom does.
chunks.st: the way that the monarchy does when a king sentences a person to death.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehudah says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says:

chunks.en: that is a disgrace.
chunks.st: This manner of execution is improper, as it degrades him.

chunks.he: אֶלָּא מַנִּיחִין אֶת רֹאשׁוֹ עַל הַסַּדָּן
chunks.en: Instead, they put his head on a block
chunks.st: Rather, they place the head of the condemned on the block,

chunks.en: and cut with an axe.
chunks.st: and chop it off with a cleaver [bekofitz].

chunks.en: They said to him,
chunks.st: The Rabbis said to him:

chunks.en: "No death is more of a disgrace than that."
chunks.st: If you are concerned about his degradation, there is no death penalty more degrading than that.
chunks.stMore: It is better for him to be executed in the manner described first.

chunks.en: How the punishment of choking is done:
chunks.st: The mitzva of those who are strangled is carried out in the following manner:

chunks.he: הָיוּ מְשַׁקְּעִין אוֹתוֹ בַזֶּבֶל עַד אַרְכֻּבּוֹתָיו
chunks.en: They would stand him in soft ground up to his knees,
chunks.st: The agents of the court submerge the condemned one in dung up to his knees so he cannot move,

chunks.en: and they put a hard cloth inside a soft one
chunks.st: and one of them places a rough scarf within a soft one,

chunks.en: and wrap it around his neck.
chunks.st: and wraps it around his neck.

chunks.he: זֶה מוֹשֵׁךְ אֶצְלוֹ וְזֶה מוֹשֵׁךְ אֶצְלוֹ,
chunks.en: This one pulls toward himself and that one pulls toward himself,
chunks.st: This one, i.e., one of the witnesses, pulls the scarf toward him, and that one, the other witness, pulls it toward him,

chunks.en: until his soul goes out.
chunks.st: until the soul of the condemned one departs.

summary: This mishnah lists the people who get the punishment of stoning, like one who serves idols, breaks Shabbos, or curses his father or mother, and those who did certain forbidden relationships.

chunks.en: These are the ones who are stoned:
chunks.st: These transgressors are those who are stoned to death:

chunks.en: one who sins with his mother,
chunks.st: One who engages in intercourse with his mother;

chunks.en: or with his father's wife,
chunks.st: or with his father’s wife, even if she is not his mother;

chunks.en: or with his daughter-in-law,
chunks.st: or with his daughter-in-law;

chunks.en: or with a man,
chunks.st: or with a male;

chunks.en: or with an animal,
chunks.st: or with an animal;

chunks.en: and a woman who sins with an animal,
chunks.st: and a woman who engages in intercourse with an animal.

chunks.en: and one who curses Hashem, and one who serves idols,
chunks.st: And one who blasphemes, and one who engages in idol worship.

words.en: and the one who curses Hashem

chunks.en: and one who gives his child to the Molech,
chunks.st: And one who gives of his offspring to Molekh,

words.note: An idol that children were given to.

chunks.en: and a ba'al ov and a yidoni,
chunks.st: and a necromancer, and a sorcerer.

words.note: A kind of witchcraft that claims to talk with the dead.

chunks.en: and one who breaks Shabbos,
chunks.st: And one who desecrates Shabbat,

chunks.en: and one who curses his father or his mother,
chunks.st: and one who curses his father or his mother,

chunks.en: and one who sins with a girl who is engaged,
chunks.st: and one who engages in intercourse with a betrothed young woman,

words.note: She had kiddushin but the wedding had not happened yet.

chunks.en: and one who tempts others to serve idols, and one who leads a whole city to serve idols,
chunks.st: and an inciter who incites individuals to idol worship, and a subverter who incites an entire city to idol worship,

words.note: He tempts a person to serve idols.

words.en: and the one who leads astray
words.note: He leads a whole city to serve idols.

chunks.en: and a sorcerer, and a ben sorer u'moreh.
chunks.st: and a warlock, and a stubborn and rebellious son.

words.note: A boy who steals and eats and drinks wildly, taught in the next perek.

chunks.en: One who sins with his mother
chunks.st: The mishna elaborates: One who unwittingly engages in intercourse with his mother who is also his father’s wife

chunks.en: is chayav for her because she is his mother,
chunks.st: is liable to bring two sin-offerings for his intercourse with her: One due to the prohibition against engaging in intercourse with one’s mother

chunks.en: and because she is his father's wife.
chunks.st: and one due to the prohibition against engaging in intercourse with one’s father’s wife.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehudah says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says:

chunks.he: אֵינוֹ חַיָּב אֶלָּא מִשּׁוּם הָאֵם בִּלְבָד.
chunks.en: he is chayav only because she is his mother.
chunks.st: He is liable to bring only one sin-offering, due to the prohibition against engaging in intercourse with one’s mother.

chunks.en: One who sins with his father's wife
chunks.st: One who unwittingly engages in intercourse with his father’s wife while his father is married to her

chunks.en: is chayav because she is his father's wife
chunks.st: is liable to bring two sin-offerings: One due to the prohibition against engaging in intercourse with one’s father’s wife

chunks.en: and because she is a married woman,
chunks.st: and one due to the prohibition against engaging in intercourse with a married woman. He is liable due to the former prohibition

chunks.en: whether while his father is alive
chunks.st: both during his father’s lifetime

chunks.en: or after his father passed away,
chunks.st: and after his father’s death,

chunks.he: בֵּין מִן הָאֵרוּסִין בֵּין מִן הַנִּשּׂוּאִין.
chunks.en: whether she was only engaged or already married to him.
chunks.st: and whether the relationship between the woman and his father is one of betrothal or one of marriage.

chunks.en: One who sins with his daughter-in-law
chunks.st: Likewise, one who unwittingly engages in intercourse with his daughter-in-law during his son’s lifetime

chunks.en: is chayav because she is his daughter-in-law
chunks.st: is liable to bring two sin-offerings for his intercourse with her: One due to the prohibition against engaging in intercourse with one’s daughter-in-law,

chunks.en: and because she is a married woman,
chunks.st: and one due to the prohibition against engaging in intercourse with a married woman. The former liability applies

chunks.en: whether while his son is alive
chunks.st: both during his son’s lifetime and

chunks.en: or after his son passed away,
chunks.st: after his son’s death,

chunks.he: בֵּין מִן הָאֵרוּסִין בֵּין מִן הַנִּשּׂוּאִין.
chunks.en: whether she was only engaged or already married to him.
chunks.st: and whether the relationship between the woman and his son is one of betrothal or one of marriage.

chunks.en: One who sins with a man or with an animal,
chunks.st: A man who engages in intercourse with a male or with an animal,

chunks.en: and a woman who sins with an animal, are stoned.
chunks.st: and a woman who engages in intercourse with an animal, are executed by stoning. The animal is likewise stoned to death.

chunks.en: If the person sinned,
chunks.st: The mishna asks: If the person sinned by doing this,

chunks.en: what did the animal do wrong?
chunks.st: how did the animal sin?

chunks.en: But because a person came
chunks.st: Rather, because

chunks.en: to a terrible sin through it,
chunks.st: a calamity was caused to a person by it,

chunks.en: that is why the Torah says it shall be stoned.
chunks.st: therefore the verse states that it should be stoned, so that it does not cause another to sin.

chunks.en: Another reason:
chunks.st: Alternatively, it is

chunks.he: שֶׁלֹּא תְהֵא בְּהֵמָה עוֹבֶרֶת בַּשּׁוּק וְיֹאמְרוּ
chunks.en: so that an animal will not walk through the market, and people will say,
chunks.st: so that this animal will not pass through the marketplace, and those who see it

chunks.he: זוֹ הִיא שֶׁנִּסְקַל פְּלוֹנִי עַל יָדָהּ:
chunks.en: "This is the one because of which so-and-so was stoned."
chunks.explain: That would shame the person who was punished.
chunks.st: will say: This is the animal because of which so-and-so was stoned, and its existence would shame his memory.

summary: One who curses Hashem is only punished if he used Hashem's real name. The judges are very careful never to say the curse more than needed, and they tear their clothes when they hear it.

chunks.he: הַמְגַדֵּף אֵינוֹ חַיָּב עַד שֶׁיְּפָרֵשׁ הַשֵּׁם.
chunks.en: One who curses Hashem is not chayav unless he says Hashem's name clearly.
chunks.st: One who blasphemes, i.e., one who curses God, is not liable unless he utters the name of God and curses it.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Korchah said,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Korḥa said:

chunks.en: Every day of the case, they question the witnesses
chunks.st: On every day of a blasphemer’s trial, when the judges judge the witnesses, i.e., interrogate the witnesses,

chunks.en: using another name: "Let Yosei hit Yosei."
chunks.explain: Instead of saying Hashem's name in the curse.
chunks.st: they ask the witnesses to use an appellation for the name of God, so that they do not utter a curse of God’s name. Specifically, the witnesses would say: Let Yosei smite Yosei,
chunks.stMore: as the name Yosei has four letters in Hebrew, as does the Tetragrammaton.

chunks.en: When the case is finished,
chunks.st: When the judgment is over,
chunks.stMore: and the court votes to deem the defendant guilty,

chunks.en: they do not punish him because of the nickname.
chunks.st: they do not sentence him to death based on the testimony of the witnesses in which they used an appellation
chunks.stMore: for the name of God, without having ever heard the exact wording of the curse.

chunks.en: Instead, they send everyone outside
chunks.st: Rather, they remove all the people
chunks.stMore: who are not required to be there from the court, so that the curse is not heard publicly,

chunks.en: and they ask the oldest of the witnesses,
chunks.st: and the judges interrogate the eldest of the witnesses,

chunks.he: וְאוֹמְרִים לוֹ אֱמֹר מַה שֶּׁשָּׁמַעְתָּ בְּפֵרוּשׁ,
chunks.en: and they say to him, "Say exactly what you heard."
chunks.st: and say to him: Say what you heard explicitly.

chunks.en: And he says it.
chunks.st: And he says exactly what he heard.

chunks.en: And the judges stand on their feet
chunks.st: And the judges stand on their feet

chunks.en: and tear their clothes, and never sew them back.
chunks.explain: To show how terrible it is to curse Hashem.
chunks.st: and make a tear in their garments, as an act of mourning for the desecration of the honor of God. And they do not ever fully stitch it back together again.

chunks.en: And the second witness says, "I heard the same as him."
chunks.st: And the second witness says: I too heard as he
chunks.stMore: did, but he does not repeat the curse explicitly.

chunks.en: And the third witness says, "I heard the same as him."
chunks.st: And the third witness, in the event that there is one, says: I too heard as he
chunks.stMore: did. In this manner, the repetition of the invective sentence is limited to what is absolutely necessary.

summary: One who serves an idol in one of the ways Hashem is served, or in the idol's own special way, gets the punishment of stoning. Other kinds of honor to an idol are also forbidden, but without the death penalty.

chunks.en: One who serves idols:
chunks.st: One who worships idols is executed by stoning.

chunks.en: whether one who serves it,
chunks.st: This includes one who worships an idol,

chunks.en: or one who slaughters an animal for it,
chunks.st: and one who slaughters an animal as an idolatrous offering,

chunks.en: or one who burns incense for it,
chunks.st: and one who burns incense as an idolatrous offering,

chunks.en: or one who pours wine for it,
chunks.st: and one who pours a libation in idol worship,

chunks.en: or one who bows to it,
chunks.st: and one who bows to an idol,

chunks.en: or one who accepts it as his god,
chunks.st: and one who declares that he accepts an idol upon himself as a god,

chunks.en: or one who says to it, "You are my god."
chunks.st: and one who says to an idol: You are my god.

chunks.he: אֲבָל הַמְגַפֵּף וְהַמְנַשֵּׁק וְהַמְכַבֵּד וְהַמְּרַבֵּץ וְהַמַּרְחִיץ,
chunks.en: But one who hugs it, kisses it, cleans it, sprinkles water before it, washes it,
chunks.st: But with regard to one who hugs an idol, or one who kisses it, or one who cleans it, or one who sprays water before it, or one who washes it,

chunks.en: rubs it with oil, dresses it, or puts shoes on it,
chunks.st: or one who rubs it with oil, or one who dresses it, or one who puts its shoes on it,

words.en: the one who rubs with oil
and the one who puts shoes on

chunks.en: breaks a mitzvah of the Torah.
chunks.st: he transgresses a prohibition
chunks.stMore: but is not liable to receive capital punishment.

chunks.en: One who makes a promise in its name or swears in its name
chunks.st: With regard to one who vows in an idol’s name and one who affirms his statement by an oath in its name,

chunks.en: breaks a mitzvah of the Torah.
chunks.st: he transgresses a prohibition.

chunks.en: One who does the disgusting act for Ba'al Peor is stoned,
chunks.st: One who defecates before the idol known as Ba’al-Peor
chunks.stMore: is liable to receive capital punishment, even though defecating is a degrading act, as

words.note: An idol served in a very disgusting way.

chunks.en: because that is how it is served.
chunks.st: that is its form of worship.

chunks.en: One who throws a stone at Markulis is stoned,
chunks.st: Likewise, one who throws a stone at Mercury

words.note: An idol that people served by throwing stones at it.

chunks.en: because that is how it is served.
chunks.st: is liable to receive capital punishment, as that is its form of worship.

summary: One who gives his child to the Molech is only chayav if he does both parts of that idol's service. The mishnah also explains two kinds of witchcraft.

chunks.en: One who gives his child to the Molech
chunks.st: One who gives of his offspring to Molekh, for which one is executed by stoning,

chunks.en: is not chayav until he hands him over to the Molech
chunks.st: is not liable unless he hands over his child to the priests of Molekh

chunks.en: and passes him through the fire.
chunks.st: and passes the child through the fire.

chunks.en: If he handed him over to the Molech but did not pass him through the fire,
chunks.st: If he handed over the child to the priests of Molekh but did not pass him through the fire,

chunks.en: or passed him through the fire but did not hand him over to the Molech,
chunks.st: or if he passed him through the fire but did not hand him over to the priests of Molekh,

chunks.en: he is not chayav,
chunks.st: he is not liable,

chunks.en: until he hands him over to the Molech and passes him through the fire.
chunks.st: unless he hands the child over to the priests of Molekh and passes him through the fire.
chunks.stMore: The list of those liable to be executed by stoning includes those who practice various types of sorcery. The mishna describes them:

chunks.he: בַּעַל אוֹב זֶה פִתּוֹם הַמְדַבֵּר מִשֶּׁחְיוֹ,
chunks.en: A ba'al ov is a pisom who seems to speak from his armpit,
chunks.st: A necromancer is a pitom from whose armpit the voice of the dead appears to speak.

chunks.en: and a yidoni is one who speaks with his mouth.
chunks.st: And a sorcerer is one from whose mouth the dead appears to speak.

chunks.en: These are stoned,
chunks.st: These, the necromancer and the sorcerer, are executed by stoning,

chunks.en: and one who asks them questions breaks a mitzvah of the Torah.
chunks.st: and one who inquires about the future through them is in violation of a prohibition.

summary: One who breaks Shabbos is stoned only for a melachah that brings kareis. One who curses his father or mother is stoned only if he used Hashem's name.

chunks.en: One who breaks Shabbos
chunks.st: Also liable to be executed by stoning is one who desecrates Shabbat

chunks.en: by doing something that, done on purpose, brings kareis,
chunks.st: by performing a matter that for its intentional performance one is liable to receive karet

words.note: A punishment from Heaven of being cut off.

chunks.en: and done by mistake, needs a korban chatas.
chunks.st: and for its unwitting performance one is obligated to bring a sin-offering.

words.note: A korban brought for a sin done by mistake.

chunks.en: One who curses his father or his mother
chunks.st: One who curses his father or his mother

chunks.en: is not chayav unless he curses them with Hashem's name.
chunks.st: is not liable to be executed by stoning unless he curses them with the name of God.

chunks.en: If he cursed them using another name of Hashem,
chunks.st: If he cursed them with an appellation of the name of God,

chunks.en: Rabbi Meir says he is chayav, and the Sages say he is patur.
chunks.st: Rabbi Meir deems him liable, and the Rabbis deem him exempt.

summary: This mishnah explains exactly when the punishment of stoning is given for a forbidden relationship with an engaged girl.

chunks.en: One who sins with a girl who is engaged
chunks.st: One who engages in intercourse with a betrothed young woman

chunks.en: is not chayav unless she is a young girl,
chunks.st: is not liable to be executed by stoning unless she is a young woman, i.e., neither a minor nor an adult;

chunks.en: never married before, and engaged,
chunks.st: a virgin; betrothed but not yet married;

chunks.en: and she is still in her father's house.
chunks.st: and she lives in her father’s home, having yet to move in with her husband.

chunks.en: If two men sinned with her,
chunks.st: If two men engaged in intercourse with her,

chunks.en: the first is stoned, and the second is choked.
chunks.st: the first is liable to be executed by stoning, and the second is liable to be executed by strangulation.
chunks.stMore: The second man is executed in this manner in accordance with the halakha of one who engages in intercourse with a married or non-virgin betrothed woman, as she was no longer a virgin when he engaged in intercourse with her.

summary: A meisis is someone who tries to talk another person into serving idols. This is the only case where the court may hide witnesses to catch him. A maddiach leads a whole city to serve idols.

chunks.en: The meisis is a regular person
chunks.st: With regard to the case of an inciter, listed among those liable to be executed by stoning, this is an ordinary person, not a prophet.

chunks.en: who tempts another regular person.
chunks.st: And it is referring to one who incites an ordinary person and not a multitude of people.

chunks.he: אָמַר לוֹ יֵשׁ יִרְאָה בְמָקוֹם פְּלוֹנִי,
chunks.en: He says to him, "There is an idol in such-and-such a place.
chunks.st: What does the inciter do? He says: There is an idol in such and such a place, which

chunks.en: This is how it eats, this is how it drinks,
chunks.st: eats like this, drinks like this,

chunks.en: this is how it does good, this is how it does harm."
chunks.st: does good for its worshippers like this, and harms those who do not worship it like this.
chunks.stMore: The mishna states a principle with regard to the halakha of an inciter: With regard to

chunks.en: For everyone in the Torah who can get a death penalty,
chunks.st: all of those mentioned in the Torah who are liable to receive the death
chunks.stMore: penalty, if there are no witnesses to their transgressions,

chunks.en: we do not hide witnesses to catch them, except for this one.
chunks.st: the court does not hide witnesses in order to ensnare and punish them, except for this case of an inciter.

chunks.en: If he said it to two people, they are his witnesses,
chunks.st: The mishna elaborates: If the inciter said his words of incitement to two men, they are his witnesses, and
chunks.stMore: he does not need to be warned before the transgression;

chunks.he: מְבִיאִין אוֹתוֹ לְבֵית דִּין וְסוֹקְלִין אוֹתוֹ.
chunks.en: and they bring him to court and stone him.
chunks.st: they bring him to court and stone him.

chunks.en: If he said it to only one,
chunks.st: If he said his words of incitement to one
chunks.stMore: man alone, that man’s testimony would not be sufficient to have the inciter executed.

chunks.he: הוּא אוֹמֵר יֶשׁ לִי חֲבֵרִים רוֹצִים בְּכָךְ.
chunks.en: he says to him, "I have friends who want this too."
chunks.st: Therefore he says to the inciter: I have friends who are interested in this;
chunks.stMore: tell them too. This way there will be more witnesses.

chunks.en: If he is sly
chunks.st: The mishna continues: If the inciter is cunning,

chunks.en: and will not speak in front of them,
chunks.st: and he knows that he cannot speak in front of two men,

chunks.en: they hide witnesses for him behind the fence,
chunks.st: the court hides witnesses for him behind the fence so that he will not see them,

chunks.en: and he says to him,
chunks.st: and the man whom the inciter had previously tried to incite says to him:

chunks.en: "Say what you told me in private."
chunks.st: Say what you said to me when we were in seclusion.

chunks.en: And the meisis says it to him,
chunks.st: And the other person, the inciter, says to him again that he should worship the idol.

chunks.en: and he answers him,
chunks.st: And he says to the inciter:

chunks.en: "How can we leave our God in Heaven
chunks.st: How can we forsake our God in Heaven

chunks.en: and go and serve wood and stones?"
chunks.st: and go and worship wood and stones?

chunks.he: אִם חוֹזֵר בּוֹ, הֲרֵי זֶה מוּטָב.
chunks.en: If he takes it back, that is good.
chunks.st: If the inciter retracts his suggestion, that is good.

chunks.en: But if he says, "This is our duty,
chunks.st: But if he says: This idol worship is our duty;

chunks.en: and this is good for us,"
chunks.st: this is what suits us,

chunks.en: those standing behind the fence
chunks.st: then those standing behind the fence

chunks.he: מְבִיאִין אוֹתוֹ לְבֵית דִּין וְסוֹקְלִין אוֹתוֹ.
chunks.en: bring him to court and stone him.
chunks.st: bring him to court and have him stoned.

chunks.en: A meisis is one who says, "I will serve,"
chunks.st: The halakha of an inciter includes one who says: I shall worship idols, or one of the following statements:

chunks.en: "I will go and serve," "Let us go and serve,"
chunks.st: I shall go and worship idols, or: let us go and worship idols,

chunks.en: "I will sacrifice," "I will go and sacrifice," "Let us go and sacrifice,"
chunks.st: or: I shall sacrifice an idolatrous offering, or: I shall go and sacrifice an idolatrous offering, or: Let us go and sacrifice an idolatrous offering,

chunks.en: "I will burn incense," "I will go and burn incense," "Let us go and burn incense,"
chunks.st: or: I shall burn incense as an idolatrous offering, or: I shall go and burn incense, or: Let us go and burn incense,

chunks.en: "I will pour wine," "I will go and pour," "Let us go and pour,"
chunks.st: or: I shall pour an idolatrous libation, or: I shall go and pour a libation, or: Let us go and pour a libation,

chunks.en: "I will bow," "I will go and bow," "Let us go and bow."
chunks.st: or: I shall bow to an idol, or: I shall go and bow, or: Let us go and bow.

chunks.en: The maddiach is one who says to many people,
chunks.st: With regard to the case of the subverter listed among those liable to be executed by stoning, this is one who says to a multitude of people:

chunks.en: "Let us go and serve idols."
chunks.st: Let us go and worship idols.

summary: A sorcerer who really does magic is stoned, but one who only fools people's eyes is not. Rabbi Akiva gives an example with two people gathering cucumbers.

chunks.en: A sorcerer who really does an act is chayav,
chunks.st: The warlock is also liable to be executed by stoning. One who performs a real act of sorcery is liable,

chunks.en: but not one who only fools the eyes.
chunks.st: but not one who deceives the eyes,
chunks.stMore: making it appear as though he is performing sorcery, as that is not considered sorcery.

words.note: Does tricks that only look like magic.

chunks.he: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ,
chunks.en: Rabbi Akiva says in the name of Rabbi Yehoshua,
chunks.st: Rabbi Akiva says in the name of Rabbi Yehoshua:

chunks.en: two people gather cucumbers by magic.
chunks.st: For example, two people can each gather cucumbers by sorcery.

chunks.he: אֶחָד לוֹקֵט פָּטוּר וְאֶחָד לוֹקֵט חַיָּב,
chunks.en: One who gathers is patur, and one who gathers is chayav.
chunks.st: One of them gathers cucumbers and he is exempt, and the other one gathers cucumbers and he is liable.

chunks.en: The one who really does an act is chayav,
chunks.st: How so? The one who performs a real act of sorcery is liable,

chunks.en: the one who only fools the eyes is patur.
chunks.st: and the one who deceives the eyes is exempt.
